test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 26 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following options represents two successive discounts that are equivalent to a single discount of 84%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Discount Formula**: Net Discount = x + y − (x × y)/100

For 20% and 80%: Net Discount = 20 + 80 − (20 × 80)/100

⇒ Net Discount = 100 − (1600/100) = 100 − 16 = 84%

This matches the required single discount of 84%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% and 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Net discount = 84%. Let the **Marked Price** (MP) = 100 units.

**Formula Used:** Final Selling Price = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a73fc6a420e6e641c871321b4c6ca13012f99c82b59fa2b70358919bc8ef54e.png] 

⇒ Let **Marked Price** = ₹100

⇒ Value after 1st discount of 20% = 100 − (20% of 100) = ₹80

⇒ Value after 2ⁿd discount of 80% = 80 − (80% of 80) = 80 − 64 = ₹16

⇒ Total Discount amount = 100 − 16 = ₹84

⇒ Net Discount percentage = (84/100) × 100 = 84%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% and 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two discounts d₁ and d₂, the single equivalent discount is calculated as [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

Order of Discounts

The final **Selling Price** remains the same regardless of the order in which successive discounts are applied (e.g., 20% then 80% is the same as 80% then 20%).

Multiple Successive Discounts

If there are three discounts a, b, and c, the net multiplier for the **Selling Price** is (1 − a/100) × (1 − b/100) × (1 − c/100).
